+## #2855 - Catalog metadata and operation example links
+
+**Decided.** Each catalog case has a required `case.toml`. `kinds` uses the
+canonical display names read from the bounded `KindInfo::ALL` source table.
+`machine` and `expect` are required descriptive strings, not executable checks.
+The flat TOML format accepts quoted strings and arrays, comments and multiline
+arrays. It refuses escapes, unsupported syntax, duplicate or empty values,
+unknown fields and unknown kinds.
+
+Every known operation-kind heading gets a deterministic marked Example cases
+block, including a placeholder when no case exists. Turning headings use an
+explicit alias map where their prose titles differ from registry names. Links
+point to the canonical GitHub source folder for each case. The generator
+preserves surrounding prose and refuses malformed blocks or missing headings
+before writing partial guide updates.
+
+Metadata and links are checked across the whole catalog even with `--case`.
+The default and rebuild commands regenerate the lists. Screenshot-only and
+PDF-only commands leave the guide unchanged. `--check` validates the metadata
+and links without writing, before building the CLI. Existing NC rebuilding and
+byte-for-byte parity checks stay unchanged.
+
+**Why.** A separate metadata file keeps case READMEs readable and gives the
+catalog one source for guide links. Reading the registry source avoids a second
+kind list and an app dependency in the small process tool. Early diagnostics
+name metadata and link problems before an expensive CLI build. Validating all
+links avoids making a filtered case command silently accept broken guide pages.
+
+**Considered and dropped.** Embedding machine-readable fields in READMEs would
+mix prose with tooling input. A new app dependency or TOML dependency would
+change Cargo dependencies for a small flat schema. A separate links-only CLI
+would add another workflow when the existing catalog commands can generate and
+check the lists. Treating `machine` or `expect` as executable assertions would
+duplicate the build script and its verification checks.
+
+**Cost to change later.** The metadata reader, guide generator and turning alias
+map are isolated in xtask. Supporting richer TOML later requires extending or
+replacing the reader and its tests; existing flat metadata remains valid.
+Changing link destinations requires regenerating the marked guide blocks.

+## #2856 - A catalog case can expect a refusal
+
+**Decided.** The `expect` field of `case.toml` takes one of two values:
+`"post"` or `"refusal"`. #2855 (PR #3139) read `expect` as a free-text
+description. This change narrows it to the two values that #2856 specifies,
+and the 12 existing cases change to `expect = "post"`. The field stays
+required, as #3139 made it: each case has a `case.toml`, so a default value
+never applies.
+
+A refusal case has no `<case>.nc`. It has `refusal.txt`. Its script saves the
+project, then runs the refused step without a catch, so the run ends with an
+error. `refusal.txt` holds the `errors` lines that the script host records,
+one line each. The CLI prints each line after `camcraft-cli: `; the file holds
+the lines without that prefix. The readers skip the other stderr lines: they
+are the log, and their times change on each run.
+
+- The app test `regenerates` opens the saved project in the script host
+  (`script::run`: `cam.load`, `cam.generate`, `cam.post`) and compares
+  `ScriptOutcome::errors` with `refusal.txt`.
+- The app test `rebuilds` runs `build.camscript` with `camcraft-cli`. It
+  requires a failed exit, a saved project, no program, and the same lines.
+- `cargo xtask catalog --check` does the same check as `rebuilds`.
+  `cargo xtask catalog` (rebuild) writes `refusal.txt` from the run.
+- A refusal case with a `.nc` file fails the layout check.
+
+The first refusal case is `2d/drill-overfeed`: a Drill fed at 400 mm/min,
+above the feed of its tool. The post refuses it by the #2598 clause.
+
+**Why.** The issue names `expect = "post" | "refusal"`. A closed set lets the
+tools act on the field. The free text that #3139 held duplicated the README.
+The script host's `errors` list is the record that the host keeps for each
+run, also for a caught refusal. The CLI prints the same list. So the two
+tests and `--check` compare one record, and the host law does not change.
+The overfeed refusal is deterministic, fast, and comes from one named law.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- A second key (for example `result`) next to the free-text `expect`: the
+  issue names `expect`, and two fields would say the same thing.
+- An optional `expect` with the default `"post"`: #3139 requires all three
+  fields, and a required field keeps one rule for each key.
+- In-process `posting::post_setup_unwritten` in `regenerates`: its error text
+  is not the line that the script host records (no `post: ` prefix, and a
+  different entry point), so the two tests could disagree.
+- A gouge or a machine-limit refusal for the first case: a gouge needs a
+  larger model, and a limit refusal depends on the machine file.
+
+**Cost to change later.** A third `expect` value needs a branch in
+`xtask/src/catalog.rs`, `xtask/src/catalog_refusal.rs` and
+`crates/app/tests/example_catalog/refusal.rs`. A change of the CLI's
+`camcraft-cli: ` prefix changes one constant in each of the two readers.

+# Drill Overfeed (a refused post)
+
+An 80 x 50 x 10 mm original test plate with two 6 mm through-holes at `(±25, 0)`.
+This case shows a refusal: CamCraft does not post the program.
+
+## What it shows
+
+1. **Drill (`Drill1`, `DR-0600`):** The operation drills the two holes. Its feed and plunge feed are 400 mm/min.
+   That is above the feed that the tool states for the work material (#2598).
+2. The operation generates. The post refuses the program and names the operation and the feed.
+   No NC program is written.
+
+The script saves `drill-overfeed.camproj` before it asks for the post.
+Open the project and post it to see the same refusal.
+Lower the feed of `Drill1` to the tool's feed, or raise the tool's feed, to clear the refusal.
+
+## Files
+
+- `model/gen_drill_overfeed_obj.py` — generator for the watertight plate mesh.
+- `model/drill-overfeed.obj` — generated mesh imported by `build.camscript`.
+- `build.camscript` — headless script that builds and saves `drill-overfeed.camproj`, then asks for the post.
+- `case.toml` — `expect = "refusal"`: the case result is a refusal, not a program.
+- `drill-overfeed.camproj` — committed project file.
+- `refusal.txt` — the refusal lines of the script run, compared byte for byte in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.
+
+## Rebuild and verify
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/drill-overfeed
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog catalog_2d_drill_overfeed
+```

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regenerate drill-overfeed.obj, the model of the catalog refusal case.
+
+The part is an original CamCraft fixture: an 80 x 50 x 10 mm plate with two
+through-bores at (+/-25, 0). Each bore is a 6.4 mm square: the envelope of
+the 6 mm drilled hole with 0.2 mm clearance. The verify gate compares the
+cut volume with the model solid, so the model carries the voids.
+
+Method: the solid is a set of grid cells over one plane set. Each face
+between an inside cell and an outside cell becomes one quad, oriented
+outward. The cells tile each plane the same way from both sides, so the
+mesh is watertight and has no T-junctions. The script checks that each
+edge is used exactly twice, in opposite directions, before it writes.
+
+Usage: python gen_drill_overfeed_obj.py [output.obj]
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+HALF_X, HALF_Y, TOP = 40.0, 25.0, 10.0
+BORE_HALF = 3.2
+BORE_X = (-25.0, 25.0)
+
+XS = sorted({-HALF_X, HALF_X} | {c + s * BORE_HALF for c in BORE_X for s in (-1, 1)})
+YS = [-HALF_Y, -BORE_HALF, BORE_HALF, HALF_Y]
+ZS = [0.0, TOP]
+PLANES = [XS, YS, ZS]
+
+
+def solid(p):
+    in_bore = any(abs(p[0] - c) < BORE_HALF for c in BORE_X) and abs(p[1]) < BORE_HALF
+    return not in_bore
+
+
+def corner(axis, plane, a, ia, b, ib):
+    pt = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
+    pt[axis] = PLANES[axis][plane]
+    pt[a] = PLANES[a][ia]
+    pt[b] = PLANES[b][ib]
+    return tuple(pt)
+
+
+def build():
+    dims = [len(p) - 1 for p in PLANES]
+    inside = set()
+    for i in range(dims[0]):
+        for j in range(dims[1]):
+            for k in range(dims[2]):
+                mid = [(PLANES[ax][n] + PLANES[ax][n + 1]) / 2 for ax, n in enumerate((i, j, k))]
+                if solid(mid):
+                    inside.add((i, j, k))
+    quads = []
+    for cell in sorted(inside):
+        for axis in range(3):
+            for sign in (1, -1):
+                nxt = list(cell)
+                nxt[axis] += sign
+                if tuple(nxt) in inside:
+                    continue
+                plane = cell[axis] + (1 if sign > 0 else 0)
+                a, b = (d for d in range(3) if d != axis)
+                ia, ib = cell[a], cell[b]
+                ring = [corner(axis, plane, a, ia, b, ib), corner(axis, plane, a, ia + 1, b, ib),
+                        corner(axis, plane, a, ia + 1, b, ib + 1), corner(axis, plane, a, ia, b, ib + 1)]
+                # Walking a then b turns about +axis for x and z, -axis for y.
+                if sign * (1 if axis != 1 else -1) < 0:
+                    ring.reverse()
+                quads.append(ring)
+    return quads
+
+
+def check(quads):
+    edges = {}
+    for q in quads:
+        for n in range(4):
+            e = (q[n], q[(n + 1) % 4])
+            edges[e] = edges.get(e, 0) + 1
+    for (p, q), count in edges.items():
+        if count != 1 or edges.get((q, p)) != 1:
+            raise SystemExit(f"mesh is not closed at edge {p} -> {q}")
+
+
+def write(quads, path):
+    verts, index, faces = [], {}, []
+    for q in quads:
+        face = []
+        for p in q:
+            if p not in index:
+                index[p] = len(verts) + 1
+                verts.append(p)
+            face.append(index[p])
+        faces.append(face)
+    with open(path, "w", newline="\n") as f:
+        f.write("# drill-overfeed: 80 x 50 x 10 mm plate, two 6 mm through-bores\n")
+        for v in verts:
+            f.write("v {:g} {:g} {:g}\n".format(*v))
+        for face in faces:
+            f.write("f " + " ".join(str(n) for n in face) + "\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "drill-overfeed.obj"
+    mesh = build()
+    check(mesh)
+    write(mesh, out)

 - `build.camscript` — headless CamCraft script (`camcraft-cli script build.camscript` from the case directory) that creates the document via undoable commands, generates, verifies, saves `<case>.camproj`, and posts `<case>.nc`.
 - `<case>.camproj` — committed project file.
-- `<case>.nc` — committed NC program.
+- `<case>.nc` — committed NC program (a case with `expect = "post"`).
+- `refusal.txt` — committed refusal lines, in place of `<case>.nc` (a case with `expect = "refusal"`).
+- `case.toml` — operation kinds, machine and expected result; the kinds drive the guide's example links.
 - `README.md` — what the case shows, its operations/tools, and what to inspect.
 
+## Case metadata
+
+Keep the case's explanation in its README. Put its machine-readable metadata in `case.toml`:
+
+```toml
+kinds = ["Face", "2D Pocket", "Drill"]
+machine = "3-axis mill"
+expect = "post"
+```
+
+`kinds` lists the exact display names from `KindInfo::ALL` in
+`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`. Each name links the case below that kind's
+heading on the operation guide pages. A case can list several kinds; the seed
+case appears below Face, 2D Pocket and Drill. The case folder's family does not
+choose its kinds: an indexed 2D Pocket is still a 2D Pocket.
+
+`machine` describes the machine used by the case. It is a required, nonempty
+description; it does not configure the machine.
+
+`expect` is `"post"` or `"refusal"` (#2856). A post case posts `<case>.nc`, and
+the tests compare it with the committed file byte for byte. A refusal case
+shows a program that CamCraft refuses to post. It has no `<case>.nc`. Its
+script saves `<case>.camproj` and then runs the refused step without a catch,
+so the script run ends with an error. `refusal.txt` holds the refusal lines
+that the script host records, one line each: the stderr lines of the run that
+start with `camcraft-cli: `, without that prefix. The log lines on stderr are
+not part of it. The tests and `--check` compare
+them with the committed file byte for byte. A refusal case that posts fails.
+
+The supported flat TOML format has quoted strings without escapes and an array
+of quoted strings for `kinds`. Single or double quotes, comments and multiline
+arrays are supported. Empty fields, duplicate fields or kinds, unknown fields,
+unknown kind names and unsupported syntax are refused. Tables and escaped
+strings are not supported.
+
 ## Adding a new case
 
 1. Copy the seed case folder `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/` to `examples/catalog/<family>/<case>/`.
 2. Replace `model/` with your clean-room model generator and mesh.
-3. Update `build.camscript` and `README.md`, naming `<case>.camproj` and `<case>.nc`.

 4. Rebuild the case's `.camproj` and `.nc` from `build.camscript`:
    ```sh
    cargo xtask catalog --case <family>/<case>

 ## Catalog commands
 
-- `cargo xtask catalog` — rebuild every case's `<case>.camproj` and `<case>.nc` from its `build.camscript`.
-- `cargo xtask catalog --check` — verify all case layouts and check that every `build.camscript` reproduces the committed `<case>.nc` without modifying tracked files.
+- `cargo xtask catalog` — generate the operation pages' Example cases lists and rebuild every case's `<case>.camproj` and `<case>.nc` (or `refusal.txt`) from its `build.camscript`.
+- `cargo xtask catalog --check` — validate metadata and guide links, then verify all case layouts and check that every `build.camscript` reproduces the committed `<case>.nc` (or `refusal.txt`) without modifying tracked files.
 - `cargo xtask catalog --screenshots` — render PNG images via `camcraft-ui` and publish the images-only branch to `origin` (`catalog-screenshots` by default).
 - `cargo xtask catalog --pdf` — build per-case PDFs into `target/catalog-pdf/` using `pandoc` and headless Chrome.
 
+`--case <family>/<case>` limits rebuilding and NC parity checks to that case.
+Metadata and guide links are still validated for the whole catalog because
+operation pages can link several cases. A missing or stale generated list and
+a link to an unknown case make `--check` fail before the CLI build. Rebuilding
+regenerates the marked Example cases blocks and preserves the surrounding guide
+prose. Screenshot-only and PDF-only commands do not regenerate these lists.
+
 ## Catalog images
 
 The screenshot command captures the model without toolpaths, then each operation separately with the same camera.
